entries.title: Student Debt and The Spirit of Indenture
entries.key_finding: Named-frames essay: student debt as modern indenture - obligation follows the person, wage capture via garnishment/income-based repayment, no bankruptcy exit; cites the historical indenture analogy but presents NO empirical design, outcomes, or estimates.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (frame named in humanities/opinion press - founder's 'I don't know of any studies' holds for peer-reviewed studies, not the essay literature)

entries.authors: McLellan L, Kelly S et al.
entries.title: Debt Relief Reforms are not Enough to Alter the Relations of Inequality and Harm Reproduction: The Case of Education[-related debt]
entries.key_finding: Frames contemporary citizens as living in 'debt bondage' under financialization and treats education debt as harm-reproducing; relief-reform skepticism - structural relations survive discharge reforms.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (debt-bondage language applied to education debt in peer-reviewed venue)

entries.title: Not the Last Word: Are Medical School Loans Mortgages Without Houses?
entries.key_finding: Frames professional-school debt as collateral-free obligation with garnishment/tax-offset collection power and near non-dischargeability - 'mortgage without houses'; documents wage-capture mechanics of the loan structure.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (mechanics: no-collateral asset + creditor superpowers) - does not use indenture term

entries.title: The Next 'Big Short': COVID-19, Student Loan Discharge in Bankruptcy, and the SLABS Market
entries.key_finding: Documents the non-dischargeability rule as market structure: securitized student-loan assets (SLABS) priced around the no-bankruptcy-exit; systemic - risk transferred to borrowers' future wages.

entries.title: Is Student Loan Debt Discouraging Homeownership among Young Adults?
entries.key_finding: Student-loan debt delays homeownership among young adults; the canonical homeownership-delay study - 60+ citations.

entries.title: Do student loans delay marriage? Debt repayment and family formation in young adulthood
entries.key_finding: Student-loan repayment burdens delay marriage and family formation in young adulthood - the canonical family-formation-delay study (42+ cites).

entries.title: Delayed Dreams: How Student Loan Debt Shapes Family Formation and Homeownership Among Liberal Arts Graduates (+ related 2026 AERA undergraduate-major/salary/debt-to-homeownership paper)
entries.venue: International journal of education & humanities (IJEH); AERA annual proceedings
entries.key_finding: Recent studies combine BOTH civic outcomes (family formation + homeownership) under student-debt delay - confirms the joint-frame is emerging but in low-visibility venues, not causal designs.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (joint frame emerging descriptively; no causal indenture-mechanism test)

entries.title: Student Debt, Homeownership, and Wealth Accumulation over the Life Cycle
entries.key_finding: Life-cycle modeling: student debt overhang lowers homeownership and wealth accumulation causally; also 'Student debt overhang: imprint on homeownership and the economy' (Business Economics 2020).
entries.design: Structural life-cycle model + quasi-experimental debt variation

entries.title: Student loan debt and mental health: a comprehensive review of scholarly literature from 1900 to 2019
entries.key_finding: Century-spanning systematic review: student-loan debt is consistently associated with adverse mental-health outcomes; reviews 120 years of published literature.
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (MH outcome of educational debt, review canon)

entries.authors: Walsemann KM, Ailshire JA et al. (PMID 33891530)
entries.title: Student loans, mental health, and substance use: A gender comparison among US young adults
entries.key_finding: Student-loan debt associated with worse mental health and higher substance use; women borrow more and suffer larger mental-health penalties - gendered indenture burden.

entries.title: The association between student loan debt and perceived socioeconomic status and problematic drinking and mental [health]
entries.key_finding: Student-loan debt lowers perceived SES; lowered SES mediates problematic drinking and mental-health strain - a status-channel mechanism within the indenture frame.

entries.authors: (PMID 42005576 - abstract failed twice via EPMC; record-level only)
entries.title: A systematic review examining the relationship between debt and the mental health outcomes of anxiety, depression [and suicidality]
entries.key_finding: Systematic review spanning ALL debt types to anxiety/depression outcomes - debt-as-class-stratifier frame at review level.
entries.confidence: medium (abstract unavailable via EPMC at time of pull - secondhand)

entries.title: Student loan debt and the career choices of college graduates with majors in the arts
entries.key_finding: Student-loan debt pushes arts graduates toward higher-paying, non-preferred careers - the career-distortion test the founder's frame predicts; earnings-drag channel measured directly.
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (measured career distortion, single cohort/major slice; no indenture-mechanism framing)

entries.title: Unequally Indebted: Debt by Education, Race, and Ethnicity and the Accumulation of Inequality in Emerging Adulthood
entries.key_finding: Debt burden stratified by education/race/ethnicity and linked to inequality accumulation in emerging adulthood - distributional evidence for the indenture frame.

entries.title: Rising nonmarital first childbearing among college-educated women: Evidence from three national studies
entries.key_finding: College-educated women's fertility timing shifted toward nonmarital first childbearing - education/debt-era family-formation backdrop (adjacent evidence on the family-formation thread).
entries.novelty_verdict: EXTENDED (family-formation outcome adjacent; debt not isolated)
entries.effect_size: tempo/timing shifts across three national studies

entries.title: Educational Expansions and Fertility: Evidence from Norwegian College Reforms
entries.key_finding: Quasi-experimental college expansion reduces/re-times fertility - education-vs-family-formation causal link exists internationally (treatment = education access, not debt burden itself).
entries.novelty_verdict: VERIFIED (education-fertility causal canon; treatment is expansion, not debt)

entries.title: Debts and experienced financial scarcity: associations with nonsuicidal self-injury and suicidality in adolescents
entries.key_finding: Debt and financial scarcity link to self-injury and suicidality in adolescents - the harm-extreme end of the debt-MH continuum, pre-dating student loans.

summary: Novelty verdict summary (SCAN-13, founder's-DEBT-REFRAME): The MECHANICS are deeply VERIFIED - non-dischargeability as market structure (PPR284205 SLABS), wage-capture/garniture framing ('mortgages without houses', PMID 37909914), home-ownership-delay canon (Houle & Berger 2015, 60+ cites) and family-formation-delay canon (Demographic Research 2014, 42+ cites) plus century-scale MH-review (PMID 38179674) and career-distortion measurement (PMID 38625166). The FRAME ITSELF ('indentured servitude' as a name for the structure) exists in the humanities/OPINION press - Dissent 2008 'Student Debt and The Spirit of Indenture' (5 cites), debt-bondage language inside an education-debt harm-reproduction paper (PMID 33424234) - but NO peer-reviewed study operationalizes the indenture structure (person-following obligation + wage capture + no bankruptcy exit) as a single NAMED mechanism and tests its civic-outcome link as one design. => Founder's intuition HOLDS in the peer-reviewed sense: named-frame essays VERIFIED (2008 Dissent origin, pre-dating the founder's framing), integrated indenture-as-mechanism with civic outcomes = NOVEL-ANGLE-leaning-GAP. Component outcomes each individually VERIFIED.
